title: The Secret Inside an Atom
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about the structure of an atom — protons, neutrons, electrons, and the scientists who discovered them.

questions.prompt: Which three subatomic particles make up an atom?
choices: Protons, molecules, and electrons
Protons, neutrons, and electrons
Neutrons, atoms, and molecules
Electrons, ions, and molecules
questions.explanation: An atom is made of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

questions.prompt: What did J. J. Thomson discover through his cathode ray experiments?
choices: Atoms contain a small, dense nucleus.
Atoms are mostly empty space.
Cathode rays contain negatively charged particles called electrons.
Neutrons have no electric charge.
questions.explanation: Thomson showed that cathode rays contain negatively charged particles called electrons.

questions.prompt: What did Eugen Goldstein observe in his experiments?
choices: Negatively charged cathode rays
Positively charged canal rays or anode rays
Neutrons inside the nucleus
Electrons orbiting the nucleus
questions.explanation: Goldstein observed positively charged canal rays, also called anode rays.

questions.prompt: What did Ernest Rutherford discover through his gold foil experiment and later research?
choices: Atoms are solid spheres without empty space.
Electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere.
Neutrons are found inside the nucleus.
Atoms are mostly empty space with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, and he later identified the proton.
questions.explanation: Rutherford showed that atoms are mostly empty space with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, and he later identified the proton.

questions.prompt: What makes an atom electrically neutral?
choices: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
It has equal numbers of neutrons and electrons.
It contains more electrons than protons.
It contains only particles without electric charge.
questions.explanation: An atom is electrically neutral when it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
